questions.question: Describe a time you took initiative beyond your job description.
strongAnswerIncludes: A measurable result and what you learned
questions.answerOutline: Situation (1-2 sentences) → Task → Action (2-3 concrete steps you took) → Result (quantified) → Lesson.

questions.question: What makes a good code review, as author and reviewer?
strongAnswerIncludes: Clear explanation of the underlying concept
Awareness of edge cases and alternatives
questions.answerOutline: Define it → give a concrete example → discuss trade-offs → mention a time you used it.

questions.question: Your top two priorities conflict and you cannot do both this week. What do you do?
strongAnswerIncludes: A clear decision and how you would measure success
questions.answerOutline: Restate the problem → list options → pick one with reasons → say how you would verify it worked.

questions.question: Design a notification service that sends millions of messages a day.
strongAnswerIncludes: A high-level design with the main components
Trade-offs, bottlenecks and how you would scale or monitor
questions.answerOutline: Clarify requirements → estimate scale → sketch components and data flow → deep-dive the riskiest part → trade-offs and monitoring.

questions.question: How do you stay current in your field?
strongAnswerIncludes: Alignment of your values with the team
A concrete example that shows it
questions.answerOutline: Answer directly → support with a short story → connect to what you want from the team.

tips: Prepare 5 stories from your experience that can be adapted to many behavioural questions.
Practise answers out loud and time them to roughly 90-150 seconds.
Show how you learn: describe what you tried, what failed and what you changed.
